clue.text: In scientific study trip miss coach; pity!

indicators.note: a trip here is a stumble, so the letters that follow lose their footing and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A disappointed traveller laments missing the coach on a field trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey sitting with 'coach', but it is the signal to rearrange MISS COACH PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of science studies the structure and behaviour of atoms, so it is a scientific study.

clue.text: Showing a slight tinge, metal smoked, keeping temperature well up

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word is placed inside the other
well up says the inserted letter sits high in the word, close to its top in this down light

parts.note: smoked fish or meat has been cured

explanation.surface: A description of smoked metal kept very hot until it takes on colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts T inside CURED, and 'well up' places it near the start: C-T-URED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinctured means faintly coloured or tinted, an adjective of slight tinge.

clue.text: Graphically transform most of pain relief

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its tail, keeping only the larger front part

parts.note: morphine is a powerful painkiller

explanation.surface: An instruction to animate a medical diagram of painkillers.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop INE from MORPHINE, the drug, to leave the first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In computer graphics, to morph is to change one image smoothly into another.

clue.text: Lying undisturbed at first in peaceful state

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the word for peaceful

parts.note: peaceful means calm

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word undisturbed is used

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone lies at rest, untroubled, in a tranquil place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like resting, but it means telling falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is false and slanderous statement, so it is a noun for untruthful talk.

clue.text: Cry of joy as overweight girl takes on husband

indicators.note: takes on here means the girl's pieces take on a letter at the front

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for larger people
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A large girl cries out happily as she acquires a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of praise or adoration, especially in worship.

clue.text: Appropriate person looking for most prosperous area of the country?

parts.words: most prosperous area of the country
parts.note: SE is the South East of England, the richest region of Britain
a quester is someone on a quest, searching for something

explanation.surface: A question about who goes seeking England's wealthiest region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here: to seize or take possession of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester is to confiscate or take possession of, the verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Punch hole in cloth

parts.note: to punch someone on the chin is to chin them
the letter O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a hole in some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like making a hole, but it gives CHIN, a verb for hitting on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing twill cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: Grunt, adjusting corset — it's no business of the state!

parts.note: a grunt is slang for a low-ranking soldier, a private

indicators.note: adjusting means setting differently, so the letters of corset are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier fiddles with his corset and insists it is nobody's concern.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector is the part of an economy run by private enterprise rather than government.

clue.text: "Pooch! That sweet sauce!", as Spooner might do well to say

indicators.note: Spooner, an Oxford don, swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds here change places

parts.note: a mutt is a dog, a pooch
that is a pointing word; the definite article fills the same role
custard is a sweet sauce poured over puddings

explanation.surface: An exclamation pointing out a dog and a pudding sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the M and C sounds of MUTT THE CUSTARD; the doubled T in the swapped word is said as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to a required standard is an idiom meaning to succeed or perform adequately.

clue.text: Engineers new fabulous figures for property lists

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
trolls are creatures of fable

explanation.surface: Engineers construct new mythical creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means from fables, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent roll is a register of a landlord's properties and the rents due on each.

clue.text: Old mnemonic device a joke at university

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark, a joke

explanation.surface: A memory aid that started as a student joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The quipu was the knotted-cord record system of the Incas.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan knotted cords served as records and memory aids, an ancient aide-memoire.

clue.text: Legume, very hot, to eat with the others …

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so the pair of letters swallows the abbreviation

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
etc, et cetera, means and the others

explanation.surface: A pulse, served piping hot, to be eaten with everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts ETC between V and H; the ellipsis links to the next clue, which also defines a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetches are climbing plants of the pea family, grown for fodder.

clue.text: … guy has a way to avoid legume

parts.note: a guy is a man
a get-out is an escape or means of avoiding something

explanation.surface: A man has found a way to dodge eating his vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar pea, eaten pod and all, is a member of the pea family of plants.

clue.text: Force that turns English out at a yard in town

indicators.note: out means the letter for English is dropped

parts.note: torque is a twisting or rotational force

explanation.surface: A rotating force throws the English out at a yard in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: TORQUAY is a seaside resort in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Devon resort on the English Riviera is a seaside town.

clue.text: So great a number deprived of noble title?

definitions.meaning: a quantity too large to be tallied, numberless
stripped of the rank of count, a nobleman

explanation.definitionFit: Something innumerable has not been tallied; humorously, a count losing his title has been un-made.

clue.text: Where one may read the news, telling of traffic congestion

definitions.text: Where one may read the news

indicators.note: telling of means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a queue of cars, an auto queue, is traffic congestion

explanation.surface: A newsreader reports on gridlock while reading from the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A television prompter shows the script to a presenter, so newsreaders read from it.

clue.text: This on table in diner on Level 5

parts.note: a diner is a cafe
a tier is a level or layer
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Something sits on a table in a restaurant on the fifth floor.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' gives E as the fifth letter; the definition points to what sits on a cafe table.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunger coffee pot is a familiar item set on a table.

clue.text: Led astray and misused a month back

parts.note: read as mis-used: the word used inside it is put wrongly together, giving a jumble of its four letters

indicators.note: back means the month's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: Someone tempted and abused a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' does double duty: its tail, used, is the anagram fodder and its prefix the signal; 'back' turns the abbreviated month.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lead someone astray, persuading them into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Top of loft in the morning frozen up: that's beside the point

indicators.note: up in a down light means read from the bottom upwards
top of means the first letter of loft, the top in a down light

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
frozen means iced

explanation.surface: The attic froze over during the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside the point' looks like irrelevant, but it means placed by the decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures to the right of the point in a number are decimal places, set beside the point.

clue.text: Time went fast, they say; it's sickening

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken, heard rather than spelt

parts.note: flew means travelled quickly

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that time has flown, and it makes them feel ill.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD as prison time comes from rhyming slang, birdlime for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian influenza is an illness, something that makes people sick.

clue.text: During drinking bout, large mixer

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letter is placed inside the bout

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree

explanation.surface: A big party animal appears during a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixer' looks like a sociable person or a drink to mix, but it is a kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidiser is a kitchen appliance that mixes ingredients.

clue.text: Cell for one on the staff, briefly, at Oxford college

parts.note: Corpus Christi is an Oxford college, known as Corpus

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a clef is a sign set on a musical staff

explanation.surface: A staff member at an Oxford college gets a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood corpuscle is a cell, red or white, carried in the blood.

clue.text: India feeds pest with a cucumber preparation

indicators.note: feeds means puts into, so the letter goes inside the word for pest

parts.note: a rat is a pest
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: India supplies a pest with a cucumber dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian side dish is made of yogurt with chopped cucumber.

clue.text: Needle, say, reversed to make lace

indicators.note: reversed means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
to tat is to make lace by hand

explanation.surface: A lacemaker's needle is turned the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a sewing tool, but it is a verb, to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or nag them, a phrasal verb of the same sense.

clue.text: Sow chews end of one waistcoat

indicators.note: chews means has in its mouth, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a gilt is a young sow

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the word one is used

explanation.surface: A pig munches the end of a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless jacket, a kind of waistcoat.

clue.text: Hesiod is truly entertaining poet

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Hesiod is, honestly, a fun poet to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Hesiod was an ancient Greek poet, which makes the definition sound like it describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, a kind of poet.

clue.text: Male deadlier when swinging the hammer here

indicators.note: swinging means moving wildly about, so the letters of deadlier are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man becomes more dangerous when he swings a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hammer' is not a tool but the malleus, one of the bones of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The malleus, called the hammer, is one of three small bones in this cavity of the ear.

clue.text: Chap in key wager collapses complex mathematical construction

parts.note: a chap is a man
Del is the delete key on a keyboard

indicators.note: in places the word for collapses inside the word for wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager
rots means decays or falls apart

explanation.surface: A man inside a key gamble falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' is a pun: the set is built from complex numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous fractal is a set of points in the complex plane, a mathematical object.
